items.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013
items.q: And then Jimmy was nice to talk to. Elvin was just sort of aloof.

ctx.x: I think Ricky Ford. I’m not sure.

Well whoever it was. And Paul looked just like McCoy Tyner. And as it turns out when he got on the road a little bit, we started trading records, as kids just out of high school. I just happened to meet him and he was with his cousin and two other black kids. We were cabbages. And we started, oh yeah, yeah, oh yeah, yeah. You collect records? I go yeah, I’ve got a lot of records, like maybe 15 hundred at the time you know, in high school. And he played a little bit, of piano, but saxophone. And so I remember the…

big Cleaners, it was a jazz night club, they called it the Royal Arms and they created a shield, you know with two blades crossing, R on one side and at the bottom was A. And there was a stage that you walked up five steps to, and it was like a semi-circle. It had a semi-circle bar and there was a space between the edge of that stage and where the three cash registers were. And you could actually fall off that stage if you got too far into the stage. And you walked up those five steps to get on the stage. So…
